direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is vast, grand, beautiful, and magical, like his other films; the direction on a microscale is decent, very Eastern; the storytelling is not the best, as he does lay out a pretty linear story but does not really do a good job establishing which side of the conflict the protagonist is on; they builds tension decently

cast.comments: Not that much of a remaining cast, but everyone plays their roles well

story.comments: The concept is pretty convoluted, as it is not clear which side of the conflict the protagonist is on, as he tries to play both sides; the plot structure is pretty linear, as opposed to other Miyazaki films; character writing is decent in that they create memorable characters, but it is not good in that the characters' motives are never clear

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is sharp and similar to his other films; the humor is similar to other Japanese animated films; the symbolism is very strong, as the movie has very strong anti-capitalist themes; the foreshadowing is present and does plant roots that are brought up later in the film

score.comments: Beautifully written and it creates synergy with the beautiful animation

sound.comments: Typical of other Japanese animated films from that time period

animation.comments: Beautifully animated, this movie is a testament to Miyazaki and Studio Ghibli's animation; it creates captivating and iconic worlds

review.pacing: Pacing is pretty good for the first half, but really drags in the second half; the second half could have been cut by 20 minutes
review.climax: Climax is well-animated and entertaining, but it is anticlimactic from a story standpoint, as is the ending
review.tone: The tone is the fantasy, Japanese animated tone similar to other Miyazaki/Studio Ghibli movies
review.overall: Overall, a beautifully animated movie that shows the creativity of Hayao Miyazaki and Studio Ghibli, but the movie is held back in similar ways to his other movies, as the story is not well-constructed since the protagonist tries to play both sides the entire time, despite never explaining why
